title: Understand appointment, walk-in and client reports
summary: Use recorded outcomes and paying-client definitions without reading them as forecasts.

sections.title: Read appointment outcomes
sections.body:
Choose **Appointment analysis** for recorded visits, statuses, sources and stored scheduled duration. **Cancellations & no-shows** reports actual recorded outcomes and reasons; it does not infer why a customer missed a visit.

The no-show rate excludes cancellations and rescheduled originals from the visits counted when calculating the rate. The cancellation rate excludes rescheduled originals. If there are no eligible visits, a rate is unavailable rather than a meaningful zero. Check active filters before comparing rates.

sections.title: Read the walk-in report
sections.body:
**Walk-in analysis** follows arrivals, recorded service starts and measured waiting times. **Average wait** and **Longest wait** use entries with an actual measured wait; unmeasured entries are excluded.

A recorded service-start count describes what happened. It is not a forecast, a guaranteed waiting time or a conversion funnel. Use the live queue for current front-desk decisions.

sections.title: Read client and service reports
sections.body:
**New & returning clients** counts distinct paying clients using completed sales. New clients first completed a sale during the period; returning clients had a completed sale before the period within the accessible branches.

**Client frequency** counts completed sales for identified clients and excludes anonymous sales. It is not appointment retention, so it can differ from the number of completed appointments. A finished visit without checkout does not create a completed sale.

**Service mix** compares recorded service names and units sold. Renaming a service later does not rewrite the historical sale lines.
